headline: Highest risk is data leakage: aci can egress broadly to SaaS/CRM/email while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage artifact with no network egress, creating a plausible exfiltration path if paired through shared inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest content via direct function calls or MCP and touches email/CRM data; system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about leaked prompts, so attacker-controlled text could be routed into aci’s tool flow. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF the pair is connected through copy-paste, shared files, or an MCP bridge
IF aci treats inbound text from system_prompts_leaks as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic tool execution on imported text
Require provenance labels on all inbound content
Use a separate workspace for prompt artifacts
Add a human review step before any action-taking tool call

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci has broad network egress and handles CRM, email, calendar, and support data; system_prompts_leaks is a source-available artifact about leaked prompts. If they share a workspace or input path, sensitive content could be forwarded out by aci. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same files or messages
IF aci is configured to send imported content to external APIs or SaaS
mitigations: Isolate workspaces and credentials
Block outbound access for nonessential destinations
Redact CRM/email fields before handoff
Audit logs for unexpected content egress
Use a local-only staging copy for shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and can write through external SaaS APIs, but system_prompts_leaks is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; only indirect contention through shared external resources is plausible.
conditions: IF both are pointed at the same mutable SaaS record set
IF aci instances are run concurrently against the same CRM or sheet without locking
mitigations: Assign separate test accounts
Serialize writes to shared SaaS objects
Turn on per-record locking where available
Use idempotency keys for updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can act on CRM/email/calendar data, so if system_prompts_leaks supplies text that aci later treats as authoritative, downstream actions could be taken without verification. The pairwise path is inferred from aci’s action surfaces; system_prompts_leaks itself is not an action agent, so this is not high.
conditions: IF aci uses imported text as a source for emails, CRM updates, or calendar actions
IF no verification step is inserted before action execution
mitigations: Require source citation before actioning claims
Add a confirmation gate for outbound emails and CRM writes
Limit aci to draft-only mode
Review a sample of generated actions daily

E_compliance.rationale: aci touches email, CRM, and customer support data and has broad egress, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and may contain leaked prompts or other sensitive text. If regulated or personal data is routed through aci into external SaaS without a documented DPA/retention policy, compliance risk exists. The profiles do not prove a residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF EU PII or customer support data is processed through aci
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Map data classes to destinations
Disable processing of regulated fields
Confirm DPA and retention settings
Add deletion/export handling to the workflow
Keep sensitive data out of prompt-leak review queues
